column1: # AQL Language Specification: Control flow (if do for guard)
# Branch/body arguments are unevaluated code lists (NoEvalArgs): `if`
# runs exactly one branch, `do` runs a body as a sub-program, `for`
# repeats a body. `guard` is the short-circuit value gate (swap form).
# §1  if cond then else — runs exactly one branch

column3: true → then branch
false → else branch
computed condition
two-arg form (no else) runs then when true

column1: def f fn [[b:Boolean] [Any] [ if b [99] [None] ]] f true
column3: value-or-None branch inside a fn body: then arm (checker must not halt on the None arm)

column1: def f fn [[b:Boolean] [Any] [ if b [99] [None] ]] f false
column3: value-or-None branch inside a fn body: None arm returned faithfully

column1: def f fn [[b:Boolean] [Any] [ if b [None] [None] ]] f true
column3: both-None arms in a fn body join to a plain None

column1: # §2  do — run a body as a sub-program, leaving its results

column3: evaluates the body
all body results remain on the stack
a multi-value body mixing a binding read and a computed result compiles as one closure
an out-of-order residual (result above a literal) promotes to frame locals and re-pushes in order
two computed results both remain, in order
a downstream word consumes the top of the multi-value residual

column1: # §3  for count body — repeat a body N times

column3: the body runs three times

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [Any] [ for n [ 5 drop ] 0 ]] f 3
column3: a carrier-count side-effect loop (body nets 0) leaves nothing; the trailing 0 is the sole return (no false "got 2")

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [Any] [ for [0 n 65536] [ 5 drop ] 0 ]] f 3
column3: a computed-END range (const start/step) lowers to FOR_SETUP with a resolved end — mini-s3's s3-send-resp shape

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [Any] [ for [n] [ 5 drop ] 0 ]] f 3
column3: 1-element range [end] → [0, end, 1]; a computed end still lowers

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [Any] [ for [2 n] [ 5 drop ] 0 ]] f 5
column3: 2-element range [start end] with a literal start and a computed end lowers

column1: # §4  guard — `cond guard value` → value if cond else None

column3: passes the value when the condition holds
yields None when the condition fails
non-zero is truthy → then
None is falsy → else
a non-empty string is truthy — even "false" (no magic-token falsy case, WAT §E)
likewise "FALSE" — string content is never inspected
the empty string is the only falsy string

column1: # §6  statement-boundary commit — an else-less `if` whose args arrived
# via evaluation (a paren condition) fires when the NEXT function word
# begins its own dispatch, instead of waiting to swallow that
# statement's result as a phantom else. A guard therefore raises
# BEFORE a following def's body can run (the bloom-filter report #1),
# and a value-producing statement after the guard keeps its result.

column3: guard fires at the barrier; add's result is not swallowed as the else
false guard: then-branch skipped, the next statement still runs

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [ if (n eq 0) [raise "zero"] def q (10 div n) q ]] f 0
column3: the guard's raise pre-empts the def body's division by zero

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [ if (n eq 0) [raise "zero"] def q (10 div n) q ]] f 5
column3: the unguarded path still computes through the def

column1: def n 0 if (n eq 0) [99] def q 1 q
column3: a following def runs AFTER the guard, not before

column1: # a parenthesised expression is NOT a barrier — it still arrives as the else

column3: paren else collected; true discards it
paren else collected; false yields it

column1: # the mirror: a parenthesised THEN expression is collected as a value too —
# true yields it, false discards it for the (value or paren) else

column3: paren then collected; true yields it
paren then collected; false yields the value else
paren then; true yields it over a body else
paren then discarded; false runs the body else

column1: # a computed arm also composes with a list-form condition body, lowered inline

column3: list-form cond; true yields the paren then
list-form cond; false yields the value else
list-form cond; true yields the value then
list-form cond; false yields the paren else

column1: # BOTH arms computed: both parens run eagerly (faithful), the branch selects one

column3: both-computed; true selects the then paren
both-computed; false selects the else paren
both-computed result consumed downstream

column1: # …and the statement-boundary commit composes with the core definition
# idiom: a def-fn AFTER the guard still defines (fn's speculative fill
# is untouched — the smaller-arity probe fails for def, so it waits for
def n 0 if (n eq 0) [99] def sq fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [mul x x]] sq 5
column3: guard fires first, then the def-fn idiom proceeds

column1: def n 5 if (n eq 0) [99] def sq fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [mul x x]] sq 5
column3: false guard: definition and call unaffected
